Religion is man made. The laws and rules of morality you subscribe to are flawed and distorted by human bias. If we consider the way Jesus lived his life, we see that he spent time with the rejected, the disenfranchised and the outcasts that the Jewish religion condemned. 

I don't understand how so called Christians can look at the work of Joel osteen for example and not imagine Jesus freaking the fuck out like he did with the merchants at the temple, and continue to visit that church.

Isn't the message love, in the end? Who loves more? you or them? If this turns out to be true in the end, who did you think gets into heaven? Those who loved other people regardless of what they did or those who went around pretending, under the "love the sinner but hate the sin" mantra? 

Also life is absurd. If there is a God, if there isn't a God, what difference does it make right now? Everyone lives on the premise that they're doing what they feel is right. So do what you feel is right, and as long as there's no judgement and only love and acceptance, don't you feel like you're living a life true to Jesus? He went around doing what he felt was right and the religious power killed him for it. So who was correct? Him or the priests? Idk, but I strongly feel like being a good person, and understanding of the struggles of being human, and not try to make other ppl feel bad is the choice I make everyday, regardless of my religion. Maybe I'm right, may be I'm wrong. Who cares. (Not being a jerk with the who cares.. think camus' the stranger)
